title: Sponge Divers Found a 2,000-Year-Old Machine

lines.text: This lump came off a 2,000-year-old shipwreck.
In 1900, Greek sponge divers sheltered from a storm off Antikythera.
Around 50 metres down, they found a wreck full of statues.
They worked in brass helmets, breathing air pumped down from the boat.
One diver died of the bends. Two were paralysed.
Among the bronze and marble came this corroded lump.
In 1902, it split apart, and a gear wheel showed through.
In 2005, X-ray CT scans revealed hidden gears and inscriptions.
It was a geared calculator for the sky.
It tracked the Sun and Moon, and predicted eclipses.
Nothing this complex appears again for over a thousand years.
And the men who found it were only looking for sponges.

shots.description: COLD OPEN, moving at frame 1. A fist-to-shoebox-sized lump of green-brown corroded bronze, crusted with calcareous growth, slowly rotates on a black plinth under a single cool spotlight. Faint caustic ripples play across it (memory of the sea).
shots.lighting: one cool spot from above + soft teal rim; caustic gobo

shots.description: X-RAY SWEEP: a bright scan line passes over the lump left to right; behind it the lump turns translucent blue-white and reveals interlocking toothed gear wheels inside, frozen.
shots.camera: same macro, locked; scan line moves
shots.lighting: emissive scan line; x-ray look (inverted, blue-white)

shots.description: Stormy grey sea, dusk. A small wooden sponge boat with a single mast and furled sail runs toward the lee of a rocky island. Rain streaks; spray. Map card follows: Peloponnese and Crete outlines, route line, pin on Antikythera between them.
shots.camera: wide 28 mm, low over the waves, tracking with the boat; map slides in at mid-shot
shots.lighting: storm overcast, cold; lightning flash once

shots.description: Blue-grey water at depth. A helmet diver descends on a weighted line onto a seabed slope; as silt settles, a jumble of amphorae and a bronze arm and shoulder of a statue emerge, plus pale marble figures half buried. No ship hull (the wood is long gone).
shots.camera: 35 mm descending tilt-down from diver to seabed reveal
characters: helmet diver (faceless: brass helmet with dark faceplate, grey canvas suit, lead boots, air hose)
shots.lighting: dim blue daylight from above, god rays; no torch (1900)

shots.description: On deck in the swell: two faceless crewmen turn the big flywheel of a hand air pump; the air hose snakes over the gunwale into the water. Cut-in: the brass helmet's dark faceplate below, bubbles streaming from the exhaust valve.
shots.camera: 35 mm handheld on deck (2.5 s), then 50 mm close on the helmet underwater
characters: helmet diver (faceless: brass helmet with dark faceplate, grey canvas suit, lead boots, air hose)
shots.lighting: overcast day on deck; blue gloom below

shots.description: Timeline draws on over a grey sea plate: 1900 (found) → 1901 (salvage continues). Small helmet-diver icons drop in a row along the 1901 segment, one after another.
Consequence, no injury shown: on deck a faceless diver sits slumped against the mast, helmet off beside him, a crewman's hand on his shoulder. Cut to one empty brass helmet resting on the wet deck.
shots.camera: 35 mm slow push, then 50 mm locked on the empty helmet

shots.description: Basket hauled up dripping over the gunwale: a bronze statue arm, a marble head (faceless, weathered), amphora shards... and the small corroded lump from S01, which the camera finds and pushes into.
shots.camera: 50 mm tracking with the basket, then rack focus + push to the lump

shots.description: MID-POINT TURN. A dim museum storeroom: wooden shelves, numbered trays. The lump lies in a tray; a crack runs across it and it splits into pieces with a dry snap. A desk lamp swings toward it: a single toothed gear wheel catches the light.
shots.camera: 50 mm slow push; tiny shake on the split
characters: hand of a faceless curator (gloveless 1902 sleeve)
shots.lighting: warm lamp, dark room; dust in the beam

shots.description: Modern lab: the fragment sits on a turntable inside a large grey X-ray CT cabinet; the turntable rotates; on a monitor, slices flicker past showing gear teeth and tiny lettering.
shots.camera: 28 mm slow arc around the cabinet; cut-in on the monitor
shots.lighting: cool white lab light; monitor glow

shots.description: The fragment dissolves into a clean reconstructed gear train floating in blue darkness: bronze gears meshing and turning together, a crank on the side turning them.
shots.camera: 35 mm orbit around the turning gear train
shots.lighting: warm key on bronze, blue rim; caustic shimmer

shots.description: Front face of the reconstruction: a dial with a small sun marker and a half-silver moon ball circling; the moon's pointer passes the sun's, and a dark disc slides over the sun marker (eclipse). Then a spiral back dial glows.
shots.lighting: bronze lit warm; eclipse moment dims the scene

shots.description: A timeline races from the mechanism (~100 BC) across an empty gap to a medieval astronomical clock icon (1300s). The gap is marked '1,000+ YEARS'.

LOOP: calm sea after the storm, the sponge boat at anchor in a cove; a diver's helmet breaks the surface and a hand lifts a single brown sponge. The camera sinks below the surface toward the dark seabed, ending on a dark green-brown shape in the silt that matches the S01 lump framing.
shots.camera: 28 mm surface-level, then dip below the waterline and push down
characters: helmet diver (faceless: brass helmet with dark faceplate, grey canvas suit, lead boots, air hose)
shots.lighting: clear golden afternoon; then blue underwater

loop_line: And the men who found it were only looking for sponges.
